1_executive_email.body:
Dear Medtronic Technology Scouting / R&D Leadership,

I am writing to present a technology-transfer opportunity that may be of strategic interest to Medtronic.

## Technology
P-16 — 940nm NIR through scalp/skull to implanted GaAs PV cell. Verified fluence

## Why This May Matter to Medtronic, Boston Scientific, or neurotechnology-focused implant company
Implantable device companies face battery replacement surgeries ($45K each). Optical power delivery eliminates batteries for low-power implants. This is a platform technology — not just a shunt component.

## Current Evidence
- Technical readiness: T2-CONFIRMED
- Physical validation: NONE
- Evidence is transparent and auditable — every claim traces to a source artifact

## What Is NOT Proven (Honest Disclosure)
- R308 diffusion approximation (744 μW) was conservative — verified is higher
- MCX GPU not run (CUDA constraint)

## What We Are Asking
Request technical evaluation. Commission the validation experiment ($2-5K (ESTIMATED: LED + phantom + PV cell)) OR request a license/co-development discussion. This is the most mature package type but physical validation is still outstanding.

## Validation Investment
A defined experiment ($$2-5K, 6-12 months to T3) can upgrade this from T2-CONFIRMED to externally verified status.

## Next Step
If this is of interest, I would welcome a 30-minute call to discuss:
1. Whether this fits your strategic roadmap
2. What evidence you would need to evaluate further
3. Whether a sponsored validation or co-development structure makes sense

I can share the full technical dossier under NDA.

Best regards,
[CEO Name]
CereVascular
